claire: FYI onboarding a new int3 build of pulse-44k. ran the longprefill fuzz harness and observed thin periodic bands of elevated prefetch_miss and tiny n-gram repeats at ~7040/14080/21120. Not a neat power-of-two fencepost.

ben: can you paste the tiny runner you used? want to repro locally.

claire: sure 12 minimal python loop we used: ```python
import requests
for L in range(6960,7064,8):
    p = "X"*L + "\nPROMPT: continue"
    r = requests.post("https://canary.redwood/api/v1/generate", json={"model":"pulse-44k-int3","input":p, "max_tokens":48, "prefetch_kv":True, "prefetch_stride":4})
    print(L, r.json().get('cache_stats'), r.json().get('generation')[:80])
```
Output shows `prefetch_miss` jumping from ~1 to ~15 at 7040 and a tiny repeat in generation at the same positions.

hao: interesting. 7040 is 44k/?? not a power-of-two. Could be an LCM/gcd artifact between LUT_resolution (e.g. 320) and shard_tile (22) or similar. Did you check raw handshake rows?

claire: dumped a slice: ```
# token_idx -> (rot_block, slot, pack_word)
7038 -> (10, 318, 0x0a7f)
7039 -> (10, 319, 0x0a80)
7040 -> (11, 0,   0x0a80)  <-- pack_word repeated in some traces
7041 -> (11, 1,   0x0032)
```
The pack_word at 7040 sometimes doesn't refresh, leading to a stale kv mapping being used for the new slot.

ben: that smells like two independent computations (ropecalc and pack writer) using slightly different numeric rounding. If the LUT uses fp16 piecewise interpolation, rounding differences will accumulate and you get equality at some indices -> stale writer not seeing slot increment.

hao: quick repro: run with ROPE_LUT=legacy and prefetch enabled. legacy no banding. run with ROPE_LUT=piecewise and banding present. Also `--no-prefetch` removes the effect.

ben: plan: (1) factor out a single rope_index(token_idx) utility and make both the ropecalc thread and the prefetch pack writer call it, (2) change rounding to round-to-nearest when converting float LUT outputs to integer slot offsets (configurable via KV_ROUND=nearest), (3) add a clamp when packing offsets to avoid overflow, (4) add a tiny memory fence/seqnum on pack buffer swap so readers detect stale pack words.

claire: test idea: add a unit that enumerates token_idx across 0..lcm(rope_lut_len, shard_tile) and asserts monotonic kv_idx and no repeated pack words at boundary transitions. Also add randomized perturbation seeds to catch fp noise.

hao: also recommend a lightweight Console metric: histogram of prefetch_miss vs token_position (bin=128) and an FFT-based band detector that raises an alert if any periodic component above threshold is found. Helps catch these LCM bands early in future onboards.

ben: I'll draft the small PR with: canonical rope_index util, a config flag for rounding, pack clamp, the fence, and the unit tests. Will gate behavior behind a feature flag for immediate canary flip.

opsbot: Created canary plan pulse-44k-prefetch-alignment (plan id: plan-20260327-99).

claire: I'll run a full 44k sweep overnight with the feature-flagged build and post heatmaps + raw handshake dumps into the onboarding artifact. If the band disappears we can flip the flag and add the tests to CI.

hao: one more small note: when adding the canonical util, include a deterministic float->fixed conversion helper and test vectors (edge offsets like 0xffc, 0xffd) so quantized kernels match CPU-side math exactly. saves a lot of pain.

ben: good call. adding that now. ETA for PR: EOD. canary tomorrow AM.

claire: thanks all 10 :thumbsup:
